text:
The description of Austin as a "naive empiricist" is inaccurate because his philosophy was sophisticated and focused on the complex logical structure and social functions of speech acts rather than simple observation. His work emphasized that meaning arises from context, usage, and normative rules within specific forms of life, which directly challenges simplistic empirical views. Therefore, labeling him as naive overlooks his rigorous contributions to pragmatics and the philosophy of language.
CONFIDENCE: 95
